name: Vladislav Surkov
role: Russian presidential aide, political strategist and deputy prime minister (1999–2020)
summary: Surkov advocates culturally specific, highly centralised Russian government and an expanding sphere of Russian power. His earlier sovereign-democracy programme combines national economic modernisation with social protection; later writing more openly defends political closure and expansion abroad.

notes: The review covers early speeches and economic arguments, the 2006 programme, innovation work, the 2019 state essay and interviews through 2025. Later explicit positions take precedence. His term reset proposal is narrower than unlimited re-election. Calls for a tsar describe personalised authority and do not establish hereditary succession. Claims about Ukrainian identity and Western plots are attributed positions, not accepted factual descriptions. Territorial partition rhetoric alone is not evidence for compulsory population transfer. Christian belief and speculative writing about future machines do not establish particular religious restrictions or an endorsement of algorithmic government. Neither party identity nor fictional characters supplied answers. All statement themes and remaining nulls were reviewed; no inference was used.
